misreading: Both attempts get the CFWS-run boundary rule wrong, but in different ways. F1 never records comments as CFWS runs, so 'a(x)b@c.de' is accepted and 'a(x) b@..' reports the space instead of the comment start. F2 treats a CFWS-only input's run as illegal (CfwsBoundary{0} instead of EmptyInput, since an empty cleaned sequence makes before/after-content tests both false), and it also raises EmptyLabel in a split pre-pass before earlier labels' hyphen/char errors.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The visible boundary test uses only a space between atoms; there is no comment between atoms, no CFWS-only input, and no domain with several label errors.
prevention: When a spec defines a composite term, implement checks over every member it lists and over the empty case; write a test per member.

misreading: crc16_update applies the X25 final xor 0xffff inside the incremental update function, and multi_checksums calls it once per span. The X25 register is therefore finalized after every span, empty spans included, so multi-span X25 results differ from crc16 on the concatenation.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible multi_checksums calls use a single span covering all the data, where finalizing per call equals finalizing once.
prevention: Separate incremental state updates from finalization; apply final transforms exactly once at the end, and test results across multiple chunks including empty chunks.

misreading: All attempts loop over a dimension even when the dimension paired with it is zero. transpose iterates the huge side of (0,usize::MAX) or (usize::MAX,0), mul iterates left.rows when right.cols==0, and solve loops rows to build and inspect a zero-width augmented matrix. solve also materializes the free list over 0..n before the n*f ShapeOverflow check, so huge empty shapes hang instead of returning at once or returning ShapeOverflow.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests use only tiny 1x1/2x2 matrices and never a huge-but-empty shape.
prevention: When any dimension can be zero, short-circuit before loops; bound work by actual element counts, and perform overflow checks before materializing index lists.

misreading: Under Padding::Forbidden, an '=' at group position two is held pending as R6 describes instead of being rejected at once with BadPadding. As a result 'Zg==' decodes successfully and 'Zg=A' reports the wrong offset; the Forbidden rejection is applied only at position three. Secondary: in Wrapped mode, a space or tab right after a row separator gives InvalidByte instead of BadWrap.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Forbidden appears only in a visible encode test; every visible decode uses Required or Optional padding and no whitespace after a wrap separator.
prevention: Apply mode-wide rules (e.g., 'reject X in mode M') in every branch where X can occur; write one test per mode per position.

misreading: All four attempts run their outer loop even when the inner dimension is zero. transpose iterates cols for a (0,usize::MAX) matrix and mul iterates left.rows for (usize::MAX,0)x(0,0), so they hang on huge empty shapes that R24 says must not be iterated. F1 alone also reports a missing numerator digit at text.len() even when a '/' sits there (e.g. '/5' or '-/5').
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests use only small shapes (e.g. 1x0 times 0x2); none has an extremely large dimension paired with a zero one.
prevention: Before nested loops, return early when any loop's trip count is zero so runtime depends on element count, not a huge empty dimension.

misreading: F1, F2 and F4 mishandle the inter-word space in the hyphenation rule: U must reserve the separating space but the baseline (C - current)^2 must not. F1 reserves it in both, so the baseline is too small. F2 and F4 reserve it in neither and accept fragments that push the line past width. F3 instead emits an empty string for empty or all-separator segments (including empty input) instead of no content lines.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The only visible hyphenation test breaks on an empty line with hyphen_cost 0, where neither the separator space nor the cost comparison matters; no empty segments are tested.
prevention: When a formula's terms differ in subtle inclusions (e.g., reserved spacing), compute each term separately as written and test the exact equality boundary.
